verdicts.reason: I read engine_noshow.py lines 746-757. pre_msgs counts any rider message from driver_assigned up to the arrival that matches RIDER_SELF_PLACE_PHRASES. It does not run the LATE or fault check that rider_contact_reading uses during the wait. I re-ran /tmp/a1bcheck1/scripts/pre_match.py, pre_match2.py and scen.py, plus my own /tmp/a1bcheck1/skC/c01.py, which sends the same message at 08:41 (before the arrival) and at 08:44 (during the wait). The defect A1b adds: with V08's shape (sparse GPS, statement that does not contest), 'I was at home, sorry, coming' and 'I'm at the wrong block, walking over' sent before the arrival give WEAK, R10, ESCALATE_HUMAN, HUMAN. Sent during the wait, the same words read UNCLEAR and give R9, UPHOLD, APPROVE. A message sent before the driver arrived therefore weighs more than the same message sent during the wait, and it moves the outcome and tier of an in-scope no-show case. A1 skeptics rated this kind of safe-direction escalation CRITICAL (ENG-7). In every one of these runs the rider is told the message 'says you were already at the pick-up point', and both parties are told 'the rider disputes presence'. Two qualifications. (a) Scenario (1), V06 going from AUTO to APPROVE, is not a defect against the engine's accepted design: during the wait the same mixed message reads UNCLEAR and costs an approval too, and D27 sends unsettled readings to a person. (b) 'belum sampai', 'kat rumah lagi', '我在路上' and "I'm waiting for my friend" are phrase-list false positives inherited from A1. rider_contact_reading also reads them PLACES, and during the wait they give STRONG and R7, so the suggested fix (count only PLACES) would not catch them. The fix should route a pre-arrival UNCLEAR message the way an UNCLEAR one during the wait is routed, not count it as WEAK.
